plain: To place or step in between two things or sides.

webster.text: To place between; as, to interpose a body between the sun and the earth.

more.text: To place between or among; to thrust in; to intrude, as an obstruction, interruption or inconvenience.
To offer, as aid or services, for relief or the adjustment of differences.

example.quote: To the second question it may be answered, that if the general government should interpose by virtue of this constitutional authority, it will be, of course, bound to pursue the authority.
